cards.prompt: At temperature 1, "go" has a **70%** chance after "Ready, set,". At which temperature is "go" **most likely**?

options.text: It's the same at every temperature

cards.explanation: A **low** temperature makes the top word even likelier, so at 0.2 it's "go" almost every time. At 2, the chances even out.

cards.prompt: A word has a **40%** chance. In **20** tries from the same text, how many times would you expect it?
cards.explanation: 40% is 4 in every 10, so in 20 tries you'd expect **8**. A chance is "how often", not "always".

cards.prompt: Which word is this model **most likely** to pick next?
cards.explanation: "Raining cats and **dogs**" is a common saying, so it's by far the likeliest next word. The model picks what usually comes next.

cards.prompt: In a story, the model happens to pick an unlikely word: the dog is now **purple**. What happens next?

options.text: It carries on, and later words may follow "purple"
It spots "purple" was unlikely and swaps it out
It writes on as if "purple" had never been added
It throws the story away and starts it again

cards.explanation: Once added, a word stays. The model reads **all** the text, "purple" included, so one odd pick can steer the rest of the story.

cards.prompt: Would each job be better with a **low** temperature, or a **higher** one?

items.label: Writing code that has to work

cards.explanation: Code and facts have one right answer: **low**. Names and jokes want variety: **higher**.

cards.prompt: Why can a chatbot confidently name a book that doesn't exist?

options.text: Its temperature was too low to pick the real book
It picks words that sound likely, not checked facts
It looked the book up online, on an out-of-date page
It's trained to sound clever, so it lies on purpose

cards.explanation: A title, author and summary all **sound** likely, so it writes them without checking: a hallucination. Low temperature makes it predictable, not inventive, and it doesn't look things up.

cards.prompt: You're planning a holiday, and ask a chatbot when a museum is open.

steps.text: It says the museum opens on Mondays, naming the museum's website as its source. What do you do?

choices.text: Plan a Monday visit: it named a source
choices.consequence: Chatbots can invent sources, or get the detail wrong. A source only helps if you open it.

choices.text: Open the museum's website and check the days
choices.consequence: Right: what the source really says is what counts.

choices.text: Ask again, to see if it says Monday twice
choices.consequence: It can repeat the same mistake. Check outside the chatbot.

cards.explanation: Days, dates and sources are where hallucinations hide. **Open the source** and check it really says what the chatbot claims.

cards.prompt: Match each situation to the idea it shows.

pairs.left: Learned which words come next from text
A setting turned up for wilder ideas
Names an author who never existed

cards.explanation: A **language model** learned which words come next; each next word gets a **chance**; **temperature** sets how adventurous its picks are; a **hallucination** is a confident false answer.
